original_question: What is the y coordinate of the center of mass of the isosceles right triangle of uniform areal density shown in Figure 9-C?
adapted_question: The figure shows an isosceles right triangle of uniform areal density. Its equal legs have length a = 6√2 in the coordinate axes' length units. Its hypotenuse lies on the x-axis and its right-angle vertex lies on the positive y-axis. What is the y-coordinate of its center of mass? Give your answer to two decimal places.

changes.change: Add explicit a=6√2 and axis incidence conditions already depicted.
changes.rationale: Original omitted numerical length a; scale cannot be invented on mandatory numeric [-8,8]² axes. This value yields a legible triangle wholly inside that window.
Recomputed for explicitly supplied length; source answer never reused as a coordinate constraint.

solution: With the hypotenuse on y=0 and isosceles-right apex on positive y-axis, vertices are(-6,0),(0,6),(6,0). Uniform triangle centroid is their average(0,2), so y=2.00. Each equal leg has length√72=6√2.

independent_check.method: Area first moment integration, independent of vertex-average centroid formula.
